request.query: Register as a resident and get a Finnish personal identity code (DVV)

sources.title: turku.fi
highlights: When you move permanently to Turku, you need to register as a resident of the municipality at the Digital and Population Data Services Agency
Residence permit and residence card (if you need a residence permit for Finland
Note that foreign documents must be translated into Finnish, Swedish, or English and legalized

sources.title: dvv.fi
highlights: A personal identity code is issued to a foreign citizen moving to Finland from abroad after they have been registered in the Population Information System at their own request or at the time they are granted a residence permit

sources.title: lomakkeet.dvv.fi
highlights: You will receive a Finnish personal identity code when you register

sources.title: dvv.fi
highlights: Everyone who requests a personal identity code must visit in person within 1 month of submitting the form, including children
proof of work or studies in Finland, for example, a certificate of student status or an employment contract (employee, check your right to work
Finnish identity code request (work, study) 2–3 weeks

sources.title: finmigrants.com
highlights: Book a DVV appointment before you arrive — they fill up 2-4 weeks in advance

sources.title: finlandhandbook.com
highlights: You might find that the first available slot for identity verification is three weeks away, and only after that does the 1–3 week processing clock begin
If you submit your request in August or early September, expect the DVV processing times to stretch toward the 4-to-6-week mark
If the clerk has everything they need in one go, your application can be processed in the "fast track" queue

sources.title: nordicexpat.com
highlights: If family registration matters to you, check DVV's document requirements in advance — this is the single most common cause of a wasted appointment
